newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua stock market unruffled by Oct. elections.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua stock market unruffled by Oct. elections.

text.p: Trading volume on the Nicaraguan stock market held steady in October despite general elections and turmoil arising from a delay in announcing the winners, the stock market monthly report said.

Shares worth a total of 298 million cordobas (US$34.3 million) were traded in October, little changed from the 300 million cordobas traded the previous month and almost double the 150 million cordobas in October 1995.

"We stayed even in October despite the uncertainty surrounding the elections and the fact that we were closed for three days. We could have been higher," stock market general manager Gerardo Arguello told Reuters.
Accumulated trading for 1996 as of the end of October was 2.571 billion cordobas ($295.5 million), topping the 1.964 billions cordoba traded in all of 1995.

While conservative Arnoldo Aleman almost certainly won Nicaragua's October 20 presidential vote, beating out left-wing former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega, an official winner has yet to be announced.
